# Ball carrier - design notes (generated by ball_carrier.py)

One-piece print-in-place: box, gate, hinge, snap latch and legs print together, roof down, no supports, no assembly. Moving parts are separated by a 0.4 mm gap.

Payload: 30 x 40 mm balls = 81 g. Print: 178 g at 100 % (box + legs 153 g, gate 26 g). Robot estimate: 110 g. Total 369 g.

## Capacity
Balls dropped one by one into the lowest free spot (gravity tilted 8 deg), around the posts: 30 fit inside the 105 mm tall box, so 30 have margin. Inside 199 x 140 mm.

## Stability and traction
CG of robot + full box: x = 72 mm (drive axle at 0), z = 93 mm; 50 % on the drive wheels.
Side tip-over at a_lat = 0.54 g -> max 0.89 m/s on a 150 mm radius curve, 1.26 m/s on 300 mm.

## Gate, latch and release
Opening moment on the gate about the hinge (15 mm below the floor): ball bed (Rankine K = 0.41, 48 kg/m3) 7 N.mm + down-slope weight + gate weight = 17 N.mm static, 40 N.mm with 0.5 g braking.
Snap fingers: 16 x 4 x 1.2 mm, k = 844 N/m each, bump engages 0.6 mm -> 0.94 N each at 30 mm = 56 N.mm hold (1.4x the braking case). Finger strain 0.42 % (PLA ok < 2 %).
Release: paddles 35 mm below the hinge, tower contact ~20 mm below it -> 2.8 N push; robot at stall ~5.8 N (2.0x). The paddles stick out 16 mm ahead of the arm tips; the floor edge is 9.6 mm further, over the tower.
Once the fingers let go, the balls and the gate's own weight swing it open; it stops ~110 deg open, a chute into the tower.

## Reset and loading
After a dump the side wings point up: lift one and the gate swings shut, the fingers click over the bumps. To load, open the gate, tip the robot back and pour the balls in, then close it.

## Printing (one job, no supports)
Roof down on the bed (smooth top). Walls vertical; the floor bridges <= 70 mm onto the centre rail, which bridges <= 52 mm between posts. Hinge: 45 deg cone pins and teardrop knuckles. Legs and pegs point up. Wings rise at 45 deg. Gaps 0.4 mm: if the gate is stuck after printing, flex it gently once.

Drag at 1.5 m/s: 0.021 N (0.4 % of the drive force) - negligible.

## Assumptions (change at the top of ball_carrier.py)
Balls 40 mm / 2.7 g; tower rim 50 mm, opening wider than 140 mm; chassis underside 22 mm above the floor; robot push 5.8 N.
